lines.trans: Every one of those guys is someone's precious son—bossing them around like that, I really disapprove!
My apartment remodel? Someone is taking care of every single detail for me!
Excuse me—I am a neighbor who just moved into the building today.
Oh hello, you moved in already! I move in next week.
Window-frame construction noise has been echoing loudly for a while now—do that work during daylight!
We are very sorry—the installer said this was the only hour he had free. We will wrap up shortly!
No way—do it tomorrow! You two look like newlyweds, yet people ought to have basic manners!
Pardon? We are not newlyweds! Understood—we will reschedule with the installer right away.
Whoa, talk about getting every wild misunderstanding in the book!

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Used as present adnominal (공사하는).

examples.text: 아까부터 샷시 공사하는 소리가 아주 시끄럽게 들리는데 날 밝을 때 하죠!
examples.trans: Window-frame construction noise has been echoing loudly for a while now—do that work during daylight!
Let us do that (construction) right away.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 묶어달랬니 쟤가? 자기는 손이 없어 귀한 아들한테!
examples.trans: Did that girl tell you to tie them? Does she have no hands of her own, making my precious son do it!
This expression comes from 'precious'.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: With future or present-progressive verbs, means 'right away / in a moment'.
With past-tense verbs, means 'just now'.

examples.trans: I'll be right there.
I just arrived a moment ago.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 선배님들이 그러시더라고요, 편집은 끝내는 게 아니라 멈추는 거라고.
examples.trans: My seniors told me that editing is not something you finish, it is something you merely stop.
This expression comes from 'finishing'.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 술 많이 마신 날엔 밀가루 안 먹는다고 했는데 삼선짜장을 시키셔서, 어제 생각보다 많이 마신 건 아니지 않을까요?
examples.trans: He once said he avoids flour after heavy drinking yet ordered black-bean noodles—might he have drunk less than we thought?
Here the word for 'on days when' is key.
Did you hear about this someone else's?
I was busy today because of someone else's.
Did you hear about this tomorrow?
I was busy today because of tomorrow.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Formed from 다 (all) + plural suffix -들

examples.trans: Has everyone been doing well?
Everyone, gather over here.

meanings.note: repeating an action or returning to a previous state

examples.trans: Please say that one more time.
I'll come back in a moment.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Passive form of 듣다 (to hear).

examples.trans: I hear a sound.
I hear a sound. (2)

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: used in 막을 내리다 / 막 내리다 ('to bring down the curtain', i.e., to end a show or era)

examples.trans: The performance came to an end.
The stage curtain went up.

meanings.note: Used as loanword + subject (매너가).

examples.text: 안 된다고요, 내일 해요 내일! 신혼부부들 같은데 사람들이 매너가 있어야지!
examples.trans: No way—do it tomorrow! You two look like newlyweds, yet people ought to have basic manners!
This point about manners is really important.

meanings.en: first, before others, ahead of time
meanings.note: Indicates priority in order or time.

examples.trans: It's late, so I'll head in first.
Who arrived first?

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (밝을).

examples.text: 아까부터 샷시 공사하는 소리가 아주 시끄럽게 들리는데 날 밝을 때 하죠!
examples.trans: Window-frame construction noise has been echoing loudly for a while now—do that work during daylight!
It is really bright compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Often carries surprise

examples.trans: Is it already all finished?
It's already midnight.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (det).

examples.text: 내가 이제 너한테 별 얘기를 다 한다.
examples.trans: Now I am telling you all sorts of personal stories.
Here the word for 'all kinds of' is key.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

meanings.note: Used as loanword noun (샷시).

examples.text: 대신에 이따가 일찍 퇴근해서 선배 새 아파트 가보려고요, 샷시 아저씨 오시기로 해서 짐도 갖다 놓을 겸.
examples.trans: Instead, I plan to leave early later and stop by your new apartment—the window installer is coming, and I can drop off boxes too.

examples.text: 아까부터 샷시 공사하는 소리가 아주 시끄럽게 들리는데 날 밝을 때 하죠!
examples.trans: Window-frame construction noise has been echoing loudly for a while now—do that work during daylight!

meanings.note: in expressions like 뭔 소리야? ('what are you talking about?')
audible sound made by people or things

examples.trans: Suddenly a strange sound was heard.

examples.text: 말도 안 되는 소리 하지 마.
examples.trans: Don't talk nonsense.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.
It really is noisily compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is noisily and nice.

meanings.en: to make someone do, to assign work
meanings.note: Causative verb; e.g., 일을 시키다 'to assign work'.
E.g., 치킨을 시키다 'to order fried chicken'.

examples.trans: The team leader assigned this work to me.
Shall we order pizza for dinner?

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + plural (신혼부부들).

examples.text: 안 된다고요, 내일 해요 내일! 신혼부부들 같은데 사람들이 매너가 있어야지!
examples.trans: No way—do it tomorrow! You two look like newlyweds, yet people ought to have basic manners!
This point about newlyweds is really important.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.
Did you hear about this son?
I was busy today because of son.

meanings.note: Used as noun (아저씨).

examples.text: 대신에 이따가 일찍 퇴근해서 선배 새 아파트 가보려고요, 샷시 아저씨 오시기로 해서 짐도 갖다 놓을 겸.
examples.trans: Instead, I plan to leave early later and stop by your new apartment—the window installer is coming, and I can drop off boxes too.

examples.text: 죄송합니다, 아저씨가 이때밖에 시간이 안 난다고 해서요. 금방 끝내겠습니다!
examples.trans: We are very sorry—the installer said this was the only hour he had free. We will wrap up shortly!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 변 대표랑 준모랑 서로 쌍소리 오가고 촬영장 아주 개판 됐대요.
examples.trans: They say CEO Byun and Joon-mo traded harsh words and the set turned into a total mess.
Here the word for 'completely' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (오해를).

examples.trans: Whoa, talk about getting every wild misunderstanding in the book!
This point about misunderstandings is really important.

meanings.note: Used as noun + -밖에 (이때밖에).

examples.text: 죄송합니다, 아저씨가 이때밖에 시간이 안 난다고 해서요. 금방 끝내겠습니다!
examples.trans: We are very sorry—the installer said this was the only hour he had free. We will wrap up shortly!
This point about only at this hour is really important.

meanings.note: Refers to planned events or work tasks for a day or period.

examples.trans: What is your schedule like this week?
The filming schedule changed suddenly.

meanings.note: Used as past adnominal (입주한).

examples.trans: Excuse me—I am a neighbor who just moved into the building today.
Let us do that (moved in) right away.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Used as hesitation interjection (저기).

examples.text: 아니 저기 백승찬, 너 뭐 하니? 나 지금 좀 당황스러우려고 그런다.
examples.trans: Wait, Baek Seung-chan, what are you doing? You are starting to fluster me right now.
Please pull over at the taxi stand over there.

examples.text: 저렇게 단순한 애랑 붙으면 케미가 살 수도 있단 말이지.
examples.trans: Pairing up with a simple guy like him could create great chemistry.
Today's atmosphere is truly like that.

meanings.note: Humble 1st person plural pronoun used when speaking to superiors or in formal settings.

examples.trans: We will prepare first.
Welcome to our company.

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (조율할).

examples.text: 난 여기서 홍보팀장 만나서 몇 가지 조율할 게 있으니까 넌 사진 촬영하고 신디 케어 잘하고.
examples.trans: I need to meet the PR manager here to coordinate a few details, so you shoot scouting photos and take good care of Cindy.
Let us do that (to coordinate) right away.

meanings.note: Respectful, polite adjective used to apologize in workplaces and to strangers. Formal 죄송합니다 is the standard workplace apology. RR: joesonghada.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for being late.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.

meanings.note: Used in 이번 주 (this week), 다음 주 (next week)

examples.trans: One week is seven days.
I'm going to go on a trip next week.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.
